text: lerobot_follower drives only the arm on its own bus; the follower bus rate gate keeps passing with margin.

A separate feetech bridge instance drives the swerve base servos on the second adapter, with its own serial device (stable /dev/serial/by-id path or udev rule), velocity watchdog and startup torque behaviour unchanged; swerve_controller and every base consumer work unchanged (same topics).
The second bus's servo-group config has room for a head group (pan/tilt) added by the next epic; a byte-count bus-cost test (fake bus) shows base + head fit its rate target.

Ansible: node types, ros2_nodes entries, udev/serial config, cgroup tier, metrics targets; READMEs, tests and the teleop-diagnostics skill updated; deployed and verified on the robot (arm teleop rate, swerve drive, both bus rates), least-dramatic motion first per CLAUDE.md.

The arm keeps a bus of its own.
The swerve base moves to the second bus, which will also carry the pan/tilt head servos (base + head share, arm alone).
The head may later be moved under the arm lease or the base lease: leave config room, do not implement the head.
